card.title: What was the House of Wisdom?

body.claim: Baghdad's House of Wisdom was a real library, but it was probably not the university it is often pictured as.
body.why: It was an Abbasid library in Baghdad, part of the larger Translation Movement that rendered works from Greek and Syriac into Arabic. Under Caliph al-Ma'mun (813 to 833) it became a public academy and library, and it was destroyed in the Mongol siege of 1258. Some historians argue that the image of a university with departments was built up in the 19th and early 20th centuries, and note that major translation efforts also happened elsewhere.
